claims.text: TiZrHfNbTa is an example of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Introducing 5 vol.% titanium diboride particles through powder metallurgy with optimized dispersion will improve the radiation tolerance of the RHEA.
The intervention will form a dispersion of titanium diboride particles in the RHEA.
Titanium diboride particles act as sinks for helium.
Helium trapping by titanium diboride particles reduces the formation of large helium bubbles.
Reducing large helium-bubble formation improves radiation tolerance.
Under 1 MeV He-ion irradiation at 500°C to 10 dpa, the TiB2-modified alloy will exhibit 35% less swelling than the unmodified alloy.
Under 1 MeV He-ion irradiation at 500°C to 10 dpa, the TiB2-modified alloy will exhibit 25% higher yield strength than the unmodified alloy.
The magnitudes of the swelling reduction and yield-strength increase depend on powder-metallurgy optimization and the resulting particle dispersion.
Comparing irradiated RHEA samples with and without titanium diboride particles can test the predicted changes in swelling and yield strength.
